newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Mobil Manila unit plans lube plant.
newsitem.headline: Mobil Manila unit plans lube plant.

text.p: Mobil Philippines Inc, a unit of Mobil Corp, is considering putting up a modern lubricant and chemicals manufacturing facility, service stations and an import terminal in the country, a Mobil official said on Thursday.
But Mobil Philippines president Claude Corkadel III told Reuters the company may have to wait until full deregulation of the Philippine oil industry takes place next year.

"We are looking at investments in an import terminal, a manufacturing facility with sufficient room to accommodate increased volumes and several strategically located storage depots aside from a number of Mobil-branded service stations," Corkadel said.
But he added: "Although the economy and the energy business are growing, the deregulation process is still not set up in a way that the right kind of new players are attracted."

For instance, Corkadel said the mandated 10 percent minimum inventory requirement slapped on new players is a deterrent since it will require huge investments in storage tanks and working capital when tanks will initially be underutilised.
If plans push through, the modern lubes and chemicals manufacturing facility will replace an existing lubes blending plant in Pandacan, Manila.
The new facility may be relocated elsewhere in the northern island of Luzon, Corkadel said.
